items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S2861

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public service law, in relation to the expiration of
minutes purchased with prepaid cellular telephone cards

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To conspicuously disclose expiration dates on prepaid cellular calling
cards.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Adds section 92-g to the Public Service Law to require disclosure of the
expiration date of the cellular minutes on a prepaid cellular calling
card.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

Specific large print requirements.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Although current law requires disclosure of the expiration date, such
information is often in very small print located on the back of a card
henceforth ascertaining the expiration date is often difficult.The popu-
larity of no contract prepaid cellular service is increasing and consum-
ers have a right to know the terms of use without having to search
through a myriad of disclosures and small fonts. Consumers often use the
expiration date as the critical factor in selecting a prepaid card and
as such it should be prominently displayed.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017/18 S2356A -Referred to Energy & Telecommunications
2013-2014:  S.2771-Referred to Energy & Telecommunications
2011-2012:  S.1085-Referred to Energy & Telecommunications
2009-2010:  S.7271-Referred to Energy & Telecommunications

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 40 Chapter 334
 
        MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 2861, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to the expira-
        tion of minutes purchased with prepaid cellular telephone cards"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This bill would require companies to print the expiration date on  all
prepaid  calling cards. Current law already requires that the expiration
date be printed on these cards, however, companies  print  them  on  the
back of the card in very small font. These dates are often difficult for
consumers  to  find.  This bill would require companies that offer these
cards for sale to prominently display the expiration date on the face of
the card.
 
  While I agree that consumers should have access to this information so
that they can make an informed decision  when  purchasing  these  cards,
many  cards  do  not  have  a  specific  expiration  date  when they are
produced. Such cards expire a certain number of days after  purchase  or
activation, meaning that the expiration date varies for each card. Addi-
tionally,  the bill would require the expiration date to be printed in a
font that is at least twice as big as any other font  inclusive  of  the
logo on the card.
 
  The  Legislature  has  agreed  to  address  these issues by allowing a
company to print either the expiration date or the expiration policy  on
the card.  Further, the Legislature has agreed to only require that such
language be printed in at least 14-point font. Based upon this agreement
with the Legislature, I am signing this bill.
 
  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Requires that prepaid cellular telephone cards have the expiration date of the minutes purchased printed on the card in conspicuous print.
